comment: Which R2 key backs each public path. The Worker is read against this table;
the publisher will be when it learns to write the second layout, which is
the point of keeping the table outside both. immutable: written once at a stable
key, because the append-only invariant already freezes these bytes.
stable: also at a key that does not depend on the release, but rewritten
in place. Feeds and the availability manifest may be briefly out of step
with a release. Tombstones use stable keys too, but change only on the full
takedown/restoration path; an accepted release neither copies nor rewrites them.
snapshot: rewritten under a release on every publication.
This says which key backs a path, not whether the path is served.
/release-delta.json is here because both implementations must still agree
about it while the Worker refuses to serve it. /index.json is in neither
position any more: it is a staging intermediate that no longer reaches R2
under any key, so there is nothing for the two sides to agree about.
Anything unrecognised must classify as snapshot. A path someone forgets to
add here then becomes release-keyed, which is only more expensive; calling
it immutable would silently freeze a file that changes.
